questions.question: Explain photosynthesis: what a plant needs, where it happens, and what is made. What happens to extra glucose?
questions.expected_answer: Photosynthesis happens mainly in the leaves. The plant takes in water through its roots and carbon dioxide through stomata in its leaves, and green chlorophyll traps the energy of sunlight. It makes glucose, a sugar, and gives off oxygen. Extra glucose is changed into starch and stored in leaves, stems, roots, flowers, fruits and seeds.

questions.question: Name the four nutrient groups and their jobs. What else does a balanced diet need, and name one disease caused by a poor diet.
questions.expected_answer: Carbohydrates give energy, proteins help the body grow and repair, fats and oils store energy and insulate and protect the body, and vitamins and minerals keep us healthy. A balanced diet also needs water and fibre. Diseases include kwashiorkor from too little protein, scurvy from too little vitamin C, anaemia from too little iron, and tooth decay or obesity from too much sugar.

questions.question: Explain how producers, consumers and decomposers are linked in an ecosystem.
questions.expected_answer: Producers, like green plants, make their own food using sunlight. Consumers eat other living things: herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat animals and omnivores eat both. Many food chains link up into a food web, with arrows from the food to the eater. Decomposers, mainly fungi and bacteria, break down dead plants, dead animals and dung and return nutrients to the soil, which producers use to grow again.
